key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but accelerates thermal-aging losses that extend into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive measurements can help engineers distinguish interface degradation from bulk losses when evaluating perovskite solar-cell treatments.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decays with diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced fullerene-induced interfacial recombination after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support the depth-dependent interpretation.
watch_item: Depth attribution depends on diffusion–recombination modeling, and the abstract provides no quantitative device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
